Background BLAST jobs

Source: R/blast_job.R
blast_job.Rd

parallel_blast() with background = TRUE returns a job and the search goes on in a separate process, so R stays free (and the search goes on even if the R session ends). Use these functions to follow the job and get its results:

  • blast_job() opens a job from its directory, e.g. in a new R session.

  • blast_job_status() shows the progress and the estimated time left.

  • blast_job_result() returns the results like parallel_blast(), waiting for the job to finish if wait = TRUE.

  • blast_job_cancel() stops the job.

  • blast_job_resume() restarts a job whose scheduler was stopped (e.g. the machine rebooted); finished batches are kept.

Usage

blast_job(job_dir)

blast_job_status(job)

blast_job_cancel(job)

blast_job_resume(job)

blast_job_result(job, wait = TRUE, progress = rlang::is_interactive())

Arguments

job_dir

Directory of an existing job.

job

A job returned by parallel_blast() or blast_job(), or the path to its directory.

wait

Wait for the job to finish? If FALSE and the job is not finished, blast_job_result() returns NULL.

progress

Show a progress bar while waiting.

Value

blast_job() and blast_job_resume() return the job; blast_job_status() a list of class blastr_job_status; blast_job_result() a tibble (see parallel_blast()); blast_job_cancel() the job, invisibly.

See also

Other search functions: blast_log_path(), blast_strategy(), exit_codes(), parallel_blast(), parallel_blast_hsps()

Examples

# needs BLAST+ (see install_dependencies())
if (has_blast()) {
  fasta <- system.file("extdata", "minimal_db_blast.fasta", package = "BLASTr")
  db <- file.path(tempdir(), "minimal_db_blast")
  make_blast_db(fasta, db_path = db)
  seqs <- readLines(system.file("extdata", "seqs_test.txt", package = "BLASTr"))
  job_dir <- tempfile("blastr_job_")
  job <- parallel_blast(seqs, db, background = TRUE, job_dir = job_dir)
  blast_job_status(job)
  # later, or in another R session:
  job <- blast_job(job_dir)
  res <- blast_job_result(job)
  res
}
